To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cloned high- and metastatic murine Lewis Lung tumor cells were found to be sensitive to lysis in vitro by T-lymphocytic-depleted autologous spleen cells, which were cytotoxic to other malignant and non-malignant C57BL/ 6 cells, but not to allogeneic targets.
cloned tumor cells from primary tumor sites and a lung metastatic site have the same in vitro and in vivo malignant properties, but the latter have a higher metastatic potential in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cytotoxicity of cloned tumor cells and the effector cells involved.
the development and biological properties of cloned malignant cells and the cytotoxicity of autoreactive effector cells.
the study of cloned high- or low-metastasizing murine Lewis lung carcinoma cells and their sensitivity to lysis by autoreactive cytotoxic spleen cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cloned malignant cell lines established from the primary tumor sites and a metastatic focus were found to be of equal malignancy, as determined by the growth rate, the cloning efficiency in agar, and the number of lung metastases.
the cloned line from the metastatic focus is more malignant than the two other lines but is equally sensitive to lyses by cytotoxic autologous effector cells.

the high-metastatic cell line was not more resistant to autoreactive cytotoxicity than the low-metastasis cell line, but that the high-malignancy cell line was not as sensitive to the cytotoxic effect of autoreactive cells as the low-malignancy line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cloned high-metastatic Lewis lung carcinoma cells have the same sensitivity as cloned low-metastasis cells to autoreactive cytotoxic cells.
the cytotoxic autoreactivity of spleen cells is not related to the metastatic rate of tumor cell lines.
the high- and low- metastatic tumor cell lines are equally sensitive to lyses by cytotoxic autologous spleen cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxic autoreactivity of T-cell-depleted cells from grafted mice is a general phenomenon, not limited to a specific type of tumor.
the cytotoxic activity against the three cloned lines of malignant cells from Lewis lung carcinoma is mediated by autoreactive T-lympho-cytes.
the cytotoxic autoreactivity is directed against tumor cells from different metastatic potential, but not against normal cells.
